items.title: The Five Pure-Abode Heavens for Noble Ones

items.zh: 復有諸聖，住止不共五淨宮地。謂無煩、無熱、善現、善見及色究竟。
items.en: Further, there are noble ones who dwell apart, in five pure-abode heavens not shared with ordinary beings: namely, Without Affliction, Without Heat, Skilful Appearance, Skilful Sight, and the Ultimate of Form.

items.title: How Refined Cultivation Produces the Pure Abodes

items.zh: 由軟、中、上、上勝、上極品雜熏修第四靜慮故。
items.en: Because of mixed cultivation of the fourth dhyāna to a weak, middling, superior, surpassingly superior, or utmost superior degree.

items.title: The Bodhisattva's Realm, and the Four Formless Spheres

items.zh: 復有超過淨宮大自在住處。有十地菩薩，由極熏修第十地故，得生其中。
items.en: Further, there is the abode of Great Sovereignty, surpassing even the pure-abode heavens. A bodhisattva of the tenth ground, through the utmost cultivation of that very ground, comes to be born there.

items.zh: 復次，無色界有四處所，或無處所。
items.en: Further, the formless realm comprises four places — or, in another sense, no place at all: the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception.

items.title: How Tall Are Humans, on Each of the Four Continents?

items.zh: 有情量建立者，謂贍部洲人身量不定，或時高大，或時卑小，然隨自肘三肘半量。
items.en: As for establishing beings' physical measure: the people of Jambudvīpa are not fixed in height — sometimes tall, sometimes short — yet always measuring three and a half of their own forearm-lengths.

items.zh: 東毘提訶身量決定，亦隨自肘三肘半量，身又高大。如東毘提訶如是，西瞿陀尼、北拘盧洲身量亦爾，轉復高大。
items.en: The people of Videha are fixed in height, likewise measuring three and a half of their own forearm-lengths, and are taller still. As with Videha, so with Godānīya and Uttarakuru: their height likewise measures three and a half of their own forearm-lengths, growing taller again at each step.

items.zh: 四大王眾天身量如拘盧舍四分之一。三十三天身量復增一足。帝釋身量半拘盧舍。時分天身量亦半拘盧舍。此上一切，如欲界天身量，當知漸漸各增一足。
items.en: The Four Great Kings' height is a quarter krośa. The Thirty-Three's height adds one further quarter to that. Indra's own height is half a krośa. The Time-Divisions Heaven's height is likewise half a krośa. Above this, throughout the rest of the desire-realm heavens, it should be understood that height increases by one further quarter at each step.

items.zh: 梵眾天身量半踰繕那。梵前益天身量一踰繕那。大梵天身量一踰繕那半。少光天身量二踰繕那。此上一切餘天身量各漸倍增。除無雲天。應知彼天減三踰繕那。
items.en: Brahmā's Retinue is half a yojana in height. Brahmā's Ministers, one full yojana. Great Brahmā, a yojana and a half. Lesser Light, two yojanas. Above this, every remaining heaven's height roughly doubles at each step — except the Cloudless Heaven, whose height should be understood as three yojanas less than the doubling would otherwise give.

items.title: How Tall Are Hell-Beings and Asuras — and Why the Formless Have No Height at All

items.zh: 又大那落迦身量不定。若作及增長極重惡不善業者，彼感身形其量廣大；餘則不爾。如大那落迦如是，寒那落迦、獨一那落迦、近邊那落迦、傍生、餓鬼亦爾。
items.en: Further, the great hells' beings are not fixed in height. Those who commit and compound extremely grave unwholesome karma acquire a correspondingly vast bodily form; others do not. As with the great hells, so too with the cold hells, the solitary hells, the neighbouring hells, animals, and hungry ghosts.

items.zh: 諸非天身量大小，如三十三天。當知無色界無有色故，無有身量。
items.en: The asuras' height, whether large or small, is comparable to the Thirty-Three. It should be understood that, since the formless realm has no form at all, it has no bodily measure whatsoever.

items.zh: 壽建立者，謂贍部洲人壽量不定。彼人以三十日夜為一月，十二月為一歲。或於一時壽無量歲，或於一時壽八萬歲，或於一時壽量漸減乃至十歲。
items.en: As for establishing lifespan: the people of Jambudvīpa are not fixed in their lifespan. They reckon thirty days and nights as one month, and twelve months as one year. At one time their lifespan is incalculable; at another time, eighty thousand years; and at yet another, it gradually shortens all the way down to ten years.

items.zh: 東毘提訶人壽量決定二百五十歲。西瞿陀尼人壽量決定五百歲。北拘盧洲人壽量決定千歲。
items.en: The people of Videha have a fixed lifespan of two hundred fifty years. The people of Godānīya have a fixed lifespan of five hundred years. The people of Uttarakuru have a fixed lifespan of one thousand years.

items.title: How Long Do the Desire-Realm Gods Live?

items.zh: 又人間五十歲是四大王眾天一日一夜。以此日夜，三十日夜為一月，十二月為一歲。彼諸天眾壽量五百歲。
items.en: Further, fifty human years equal a single day and night for the Four Great Kings. Reckoned by this day and night, thirty days and nights make one month, and twelve months make one year. That heaven's beings live five hundred such years.

items.zh: 人間百歲是三十三天一日一夜。以此日夜如前說，彼諸天眾壽量千歲。如是所餘，乃至他化自在天，日夜及壽量各增前一倍。
items.en: A hundred human years equal a single day and night for the Thirty-Three. Reckoned in the same way, that heaven's beings live one thousand such years. So it continues for the rest, up through the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations: each heaven's day-and-night, and its lifespan, doubles the one below it.

items.title: How Long Do Hell-Beings, Asuras, Animals, and Ghosts Live?

items.zh: 又四大王眾天滿足壽量是等活大那落迦一日一夜。即以此三十日夜為一月，十二月為一歲。彼大那落迦壽五百歲。
items.en: Further, a full lifespan of the Four Great Kings equals a single day and night in the Reviving Hell; reckoned by this, thirty days and nights make one month, twelve months make one year. That hell's beings live five hundred such years.

items.zh: 以四大王眾天壽量成等活大那落迦壽量，如是以三十三天壽量成黑繩大那落迦壽量，以時分天壽量成眾合大那落迦壽量，以知足天壽量成號叫大那落迦壽量，以樂化天壽量成大號叫大那落迦壽量，以他化自在天壽量成燒熱大那落迦壽量，應知亦爾。
items.en: Just as the Four Great Kings' lifespan produces the Reviving Hell's lifespan, so the Thirty-Three's lifespan produces the Black-Rope Hell's, the Time-Divisions Heaven's produces the Crushing Hell's, the Contentment Heaven's produces the Wailing Hell's, the Delighting-in-Transformation Heaven's produces the Great Wailing Hell's, and the Mastery-over-Others'-Transformations Heaven's produces the Burning Hell's — this should be understood in just the same way.

items.zh: 極燒熱大那落迦有情壽半中劫。無間大那落迦有情壽一中劫。
items.en: The beings of the Intensely Burning Hell live half an intermediate eon. The beings of the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering live one full intermediate eon.

items.zh: 非天壽量如三十三天。傍生、餓鬼壽量不定。又寒那落迦於大那落迦次第相望，壽量近半應知。又近邊那落迦、獨一那落迦受生有情壽量不定。
items.en: The asuras' lifespan is comparable to the Thirty-Three's. Animals' and hungry ghosts' lifespans are not fixed. The cold hells, set against the great hells in the same order, have roughly half their lifespan, it should be understood. The neighbouring hells' and solitary hells' beings have no fixed lifespan.

items.title: How Long Do Beings in the Form and Formless Realms Live?

items.zh: 梵眾天壽二十中劫一劫，梵前益天壽四十中劫一劫，大梵天壽六十中劫一劫，少光天壽八十中劫二劫。自此以上，餘色界天壽量相望，各漸倍增。唯除無雲。當知彼天壽減三劫。
items.en: Brahmā's Retinue lives for one great eon of twenty intermediate eons; Brahmā's Ministers, one great eon of forty intermediate eons; Great Brahmā, one great eon of sixty intermediate eons; Lesser Light, two great eons of eighty intermediate eons each. Above this, the remaining form-realm heavens' lifespans, set against one another, each roughly double the one before — except the Cloudless Heaven, whose lifespan should be understood as three great eons less than the doubling would otherwise give.

items.zh: 空無邊處壽二萬劫，識無邊處壽四萬劫，無所有處壽六萬劫，非想非非想處壽八萬劫。
items.en: The sphere of infinite space lives twenty thousand eons; the sphere of infinite consciousness, forty thousand eons; the sphere of nothingness, sixty thousand eons; the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, eighty thousand eons.

blocks.text: Today completes the map of the three realms and then measures them: how tall beings are and how long they live in each place. The numbers grow quickly and can be skimmed. Two points are worth slowing down for: the **pure abodes**, which only noble ones enter, and the way heavenly time dwarfs human time, which our teachers use to put a human life in perspective.

Above the ordinary fourth-dhyāna heavens are the five **pure abodes** (五淨居天), where non-returners are reborn. They come from "mixed cultivation of the fourth dhyāna" at five grades. Venerable Miào Jìng explains the mixing: an ordinary being's dhyāna carries subtle attachment, view, and conceit towards the absorption itself. The practitioner breaks this by alternating uncontaminated moments of insight into impermanence, non-self, and emptiness with contaminated moments of absorption, at first for long stretches, then shorter and shorter, down to a single moment. The finer the alternation, the higher the pure abode.
Beyond them is the abode of **Great Sovereignty** (大自在住處), where "a bodhisattva of the tenth ground, through the utmost cultivation of that very ground, comes to be born".

The formless realm has "four places, or no place at all". Venerable Miào Jìng: since it has no form, no structure of earth, water, fire, and wind, one may say it has no place; in terms of the states it manifests, one may speak of four.

The people of **Jambudvīpa** are "not fixed in height, sometimes tall, sometimes short, yet always measuring three and a half of their own forearm-lengths". Proportion is fixed; absolute size is not. The other continents' peoples are fixed and taller in order. Gods' heights grow from a quarter krośa among the Four Great Kings upwards, and in the form realm they double at each level (with one odd exception, the Cloudless Heaven, which both teachers compute as 125 yojanas). Asuras are as tall as the gods of the Thirty-Three. Hell-beings vary, vast for those who committed the gravest crimes. The formless realm has no size at all.
Human lifespans on the other continents are fixed: 250, 500, and 1,000 years. In the desire heavens, time stretches:

items: Fifty human years equal one day and night of the **Four Great Kings**, who live five hundred of their own years.
Each heaven above **doubles** the day-and-night and the lifespan of the one below.

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi tells a story to make the scale felt. A palace attendant of Indra fell to the human world, lived a life of generosity, died at fifty, and returned to the Thirty-Three. Indra asked her only: "Why haven't I seen you for half a day?" Venerable Miào Jìng adds that Maitreya will live four thousand Tuṣita years before descending to become the next Buddha.

subs.head: The hells, by the same clock

blocks.text: The hells are measured against the heavens. A whole lifespan of the Four Great Kings equals one day and night in the **Reviving Hell**, whose beings live five hundred such years; each lower hell is paired with the next heaven up. The two lowest are measured in eons: half an intermediate eon in the Intensely Burning Hell, a full intermediate eon in the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi: "the lower one goes, the longer one lives, and the longer one lives, the longer one suffers."

Lifespans there are measured in eons, up to eighty thousand eons at the peak of existence. Master Cháng Bǎi quotes a saying: "Better to be Devadatta falling into hell than to be born at the peak of existence." Devadatta at least has the Dharma to be perfumed by; at the peak one cannot hear or practise it for eighty thousand eons. Deep concentration with little wisdom is listed among the unfavourable conditions for practice.

quiz.q: The five pure abodes arise from "mixed cultivation of the fourth dhyāna" at five grades. How do the two teachers explain "mixed cultivation"?
options: alternating uncontaminated and contaminated moments of meditative mind — using uncontaminated insight into impermanence and not-self to break attachment, view, and conceit towards the absorption; the five grades of refinement yield the five pure abodes in turn
practising all four dhyānas at once
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: an ordinary being's dhyāna carries attachment, view, and conceit; one breaks them with, say, "thirty minutes" of uncontaminated insight into impermanence, not-self, and emptiness, shortening step by step to a single instant — "always two parts uncontaminated perfuming one part contaminated." Master Cháng Bǎi: uncontaminated–contaminated–uncontaminated is the weak grade; five rounds of refinement reach the utmost, fifteen moments in all, "and by these five grades of mixed cultivation one is reborn in the five pure abodes in order."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, who is born in the abode of Great Sovereignty beyond the pure abodes?
options: tenth-ground bodhisattvas, through the utmost cultivation of that ground
quiz.why: "There is the abode of Great Sovereignty, surpassing even the pure-abode heavens. A bodhisattva of the tenth ground, through the utmost cultivation of that very ground, comes to be born there." Master Cháng Bǎi: the treatise holds that tenth-ground bodhisattvas attain buddhahood there, in a reward-body; buddhahood shown in the human world is a transformation-body. Venerable Miào Jìng: buddhahood in heaven is for the Buddha's own enjoyment; in the human world, for beings' sake.

quiz.q: The treatise says the formless realm has "four places — or no place at all." According to Venerable Miào Jìng, why both?
options: in terms of the forms it manifests one may say it has places; in terms of its result, which has no form, one may say it has none — there are no palaces made of the elements
because it sometimes exists and sometimes not
because only the Buddha can see it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The formless heavens have no form, no organisation of earth, water, fire, and wind, so it is fine to say they have no place"; "in terms of what they manifest one may say they have places; in terms of the result, which is formless, one may say they have none." He adds that formless rebirth occurs right where one is. Master Cháng Bǎi cites the schools' differing views on whether "formless" excludes even subtle matter.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the height of the people of Jambudvīpa?
options: not fixed — sometimes tall, sometimes short — yet always three and a half of their own forearm-lengths
quiz.why: "The people of Jambudvīpa are not fixed in height — sometimes tall, sometimes short — yet always measuring three and a half of their own forearm-lengths." The other three continents' heights are fixed and rise in order. Master Cháng Bǎi: humans are tall at the start of an age and small when lifespans fall to ten years, but always three and a half of their own forearms; height rises south, east, west, north. C is Indra's and the Time-Divisions gods' height.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how many human years equal one day and night of the Four Great Kings, and how long do they live?
quiz.why: "Fifty human years equal a single day and night for the Four Great Kings. Reckoned by this day and night, thirty days and nights make one month, and twelve months make one year. That heaven's beings live five hundred such years." A is the Thirty-Three. Master Cháng Bǎi's conversion: the Four Great Kings' five hundred years is nine million human years; the Thirty-Three's thousand is thirty-six million.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how do day-and-night and lifespan change from the Thirty-Three up to the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations?
quiz.why: "So it continues for the rest, up through the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations: each heaven's day-and-night, and its lifespan, doubles the one below it." Master Cháng Bǎi: the Thirty-Three live 1,000 years, the Time-Divisions 2,000, Contentment 4,000, Delighting in Transformation 8,000, and Mastery over Others' Transformations 16,000.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how long do beings live in the Intensely Burning Hell and in the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering?
options: the same as the highest desire heaven
half an intermediate eon, and one full intermediate eon
quiz.why: "The beings of the Intensely Burning Hell live half an intermediate eon. The beings of the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering live one full intermediate eon." These two are no longer paired with heavens but measured in eons. B is the peak of existence. The same passage gives the asuras the Thirty-Three's lifespan, leaves animals and ghosts unfixed, and gives the cold hells roughly half of the corresponding great hells.
